newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares emboldened, hit new records.
newsitem.headline: German shares emboldened, hit new records.

text.p: German shares took heart on Wednesday, shrugging off a weak start on Wall Street in afternoon European trade to shoot ahead to new records amid comfortable liquidity conditions.
"People seem not to be afraid anymore," said a Frankfurt trader. "The dollar is up, Bunds are good: as long as the environment stays positive I can see more records ahead."

The 30-share DAX closed the bourse session up 42.69 points, or 1.14 percent, at 3,798.51 points -- a record closing high and just shy of the elusive 3,800 point level viewed as the market's next important threshold.
In after-bourse electronic trade, the IBIS DAX sprang past 3,800 to end the late session at a record 3,819.52 points, even after the Dow Jones started out with minor losses.
Dealers said the upsurge in activity was largely due to window-dressing ahead of the end of the 1997 second quarter, noting that many German funds appeared underinvested.
"At the moment this is a volume-driven market. As long as the liquidity is there, we should stand up to whatever Wall Street can throw at us," said a Munich dealer.
Deutsche Bank shares resumed their ascent from Tuesday, when a move past 100 marks triggered a wave of technically-driven buy orders.

The shares ends bourse trade up 4.80 marks at 104.30 marks, just off an alltime record of 104.50 marks and closed the late session at 104.10. Commerzbank shares followed suit to gain 1.60 marks to 50.45 marks and end IBIS at 50.15 marks.

Among other specific shares, carmaker Volkswagen AG rose 17 marks to 1,250 marks and closed IBIS at 1,249 after reaching a deal with IG Metall over wages and early-retirement guidelines for older workers.
